# Independent quaternary LP: [[544,64,14]]

This package reconstructs a binary CSS lifted product over F4[C8] from two
independent 3-by-5 constituents. Its distance is exactly 14 in both sectors,
the raw and balanced check weights are at most 9, and the displayed full regular
canonical frame has width 16. Width optimality is not claimed.

The check matrices are

    HX = (A tensor I5 | I3 tensor B^dagger)
    HZ = (I5 tensor B | A^dagger tensor I3).

The dagger reverses group exponents and transposes the matrix; it does not
Frobenius-conjugate field coefficients. Binary expansion uses the self-dual
trace basis (omega,omega^2). Entries and physical weight-14 witnesses are in
`candidate.json`. Each check combines a constituent row with a column of the
other constituent. Complementary omega/omega^2 patterns permit the weight-9
checks without the zeros needed in the self-adjoint examples.

Run a quick, read-only audit from any working directory:

```sh
python3 check.py
```

Python >= 3.10 with its standard library is sufficient. The audit reconstructs
the physical CSS code and checks ranks 240/240, dimension 64, both translated
logical kernels, the complete identity cross-Gram, common cyclic symmetry,
equivalence of search row spaces and logical detector bases, and the nontrivial
weight-14 witnesses. It checks the preserved execution records for every one of
the 68 translation roots, the absence of omitted branch partitions, and all
input, source and output hashes, and declared executable identities.

Both exhaustive runs excluded every nontrivial physical logical through
weight 13: X used 1,181,378 nodes; Z used 1,815,218 nodes. These are completed
execution records, not formal node-by-node proof traces. Executable contents are omitted; replay compiles the portable C++17 source:

```sh
python3 check.py --replay --seconds 90
```

Fresh replay compiles into a temporary directory and changes no evidence files.
An unfinished replay exits 75 and establishes no new lower bound. Each sector
receives the requested time limit; the solver checks its limit periodically.

Every package reference is relative. Public receipts retain numerical arguments,
search outcomes, coverage, and elapsed costs, with metadata normalized.
SHA256SUMS.json protects the included files, including the checker.

Public receipts have calendar, job, and workstation metadata removed. File hashes
bind the normalized copies. Executable fingerprints are declarations; compiled
binaries are omitted. Portable replay builds from the supplied source.
